newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: US says focusing on flourishing African business.
newsitem.headline: US says focusing on flourishing African business.

text.p: Business opportunities abound in Africa and the U.S. government is focusing on the continent like never before, U.S. deputy assistant secretary of state for African Affairs, Regina Brown, said on Tuesday.

"This is a particularly exciting time to be working in Africa, and the region is experiencing its highest growth in decades," she told delegates at a sub-Saharan Oil and Minerals conference. "Business opportunities in Africa abound and could grow."
Brown said economic reforms and democracy sweeping large parts of the continent had led to changes in the world's perception of Africa.
She said the U.S. would seek to support African countries, making strong efforts in trade and investor liberalisation.
"Africa, today, is the focus of the U.S. government like never before, and the principal thrust is in economic and commercial development".
But African countries would have to compete aggressively on the world market and the continent's leaders continue with economic structural reform campaigns, she said.
Brown said President Laurent Kabila's new government in the Democratic Republic of Congo could count on U.S. aid if a democracy was created and economic growth pursued.

"The new government of the Congo has a tremendous opportunity to create a participatory democracy and a prosperous economy...African nations and the rest of the international community should seek out ways to support such a transformation.
"If...the New Congo vigorously pursue growth-orientated economic policies, it could take advantage of the opportunities offered under the Clinton administration's Africa initiative," she said.
Other speakers at the conference echoed Brown's comments.
The World Bank's Indian Ocean country director Michael Sarris said exceptionally high returns on African investment have attracted investors.
"We believe at the (World) Bank that Africa is on the move," he added.
He said minerals and oil was one of the largest contributors to growth although large parts of the continent were still unexplored.
"Sub-Saharan Africa is a new frontier for direct (mining exploration) investment," Sarris said.
